voyage.name: Corteo dei Re Magi
voyage.content: A parade in Milan featuring the Biblical Three Wise Men who visited Jesus on Epiphany.

voyage.name: Plastic
voyage.content: a very special club, where he spent a lot of time from Andy Warhol to Giorgio Armani and Dolce e Gabbana. It is located in the coolest area of ​​the city, Milano Sud.

voyage.name: Milano Pride
voyage.content: a parade and festival, is held at the end of June each year.

voyage.name: Serravalle Scrivia
voyage.content: One of the biggest shopping outlets in Europe, containing 180 stores, despite being 1 hours' drive from the city and in the Piedmont region, it is definitely worth a visit if you're a shopping fan. And it has a very pleasant feel because it is more like a mini-town than an actual outlet, with Italian-style piazzas and pretty alleyways, surrounded by rolling hills and a lovely local countryside, and absent of cars. Wi

voyage.name: Duomo
voyage.price: Cathedral: adult €3; roof by stairs €13, by lift €15; Baptistery of St John €3
voyage.content: Massive, impressive and slightly mad: the cathedral is a late Gothic confection in white marble, festooned with spires and statues. You can admire the facade free from the piazza; getting inside or onto the roof involves three separate queues that may take over an hour, unless you book online. First locate the ticket office: it's along the street on the cathedral's south flank but has been known to wander, with vario

voyage.name: San Maurizio al Monastero Maggiore
voyage.content: A must-see! A stunning fully frescoed renaissance church. Most of the paintings are the work of Bernardino Luini.

voyage.name: Basilica di Sant'Ambrogio
voyage.content: A beautiful and huge Romanesque church which was almost destroyed by allied bombing in World War II, although some of its mosaics left well preserved.

voyage.name: Basilica di San Lorenzo Maggiore
voyage.content: A lovely 4th-century basilica, perhaps is one of the oldest basilicas in Western Europe. It is famous for its beautiful courtyard, with Roman-age columns and statue of the emperor Constantine. The Colonne di San Lorenzo (St. Lawrence's columns) are actually a remain of the Roman "Mediolanum", dating from the 3rd century AD. Further south the square you can see Medieval Porta Ticinese (there is also a homonymous newer

voyage.name: Museum of the 20th Century
voyage.price: Full admission €10, reduced admission €5, children 0–12 years free; first Sunday of the month, and first and third Tuesdays of the month from 2PM are also free
voyage.hours: Tue Wed Fri Sat Sun 10:00–19:30, Thu 10:00–22:30
voyage.content: "Del 900" but meaning "since 1900", this modern art museum has a rich selection of works by Modigliani, Picasso, Morandi, Boccioni and more. The upper stairwell gives a good view of the Duomo rooftop.

voyage.name: Ambrosian Gallery and Library
voyage.content: Historical library that also houses the Ambrosian art gallery with treasures such as Leonardo Atlantic Codex.

voyage.name: Civic Archeological Museum
voyage.content: Roman antiques from Milan and the surrounding area.

voyage.name: Brera Art Gallery
voyage.content: One of Italy's most important art collections and one of the foremost collections of Italian paintings. The ticketing system is a bit unusual – there are no "standard" single-entry tickets, only a "Brera card", which allows one to visit any number of times within 3 months. It costs €15, but the entry date/time slot still needs to be booked and may be sold out for the current day!

voyage.name: Scala Theater Museum
voyage.price: €12 (reduced for students and people older than 65)
voyage.content: A museum dedicated to one of the world's most famous opera houses. All types of memorabilias like dresses and pictures are on display. This includes a view into the opera hall from one of the loges, which is a short and simple alternative to the official guided tour of the opera. (Note that third party tour operators of the opera are not showing anything other than this view from the museum.) Check the museum website

voyage.name: Royal Palace
voyage.content: Always hosts many exhibitions, usually very interesting. Tickets are sold separately for each exhibition!

voyage.name: Bagatti Valsecchi Museum
voyage.price: €14; entrance is included in the Case Museo (house museums) card
voyage.content: Extraordinary, somewhat bizarre 1880s house museum of the aristocratic Bagatti Valsecchi brothers, showcasing their passion for Renaissance art and design. Slightly spoiled by unsympathetic electrical wiring and noise-generating machines.

voyage.name: Poldi Pezzoli Museum
voyage.price: €15, or included with the Casa Museo card
voyage.content: A varied collection of art from the 14th to 19th century, including armour, clocks, porcelain and tapestries. It has been a museum since 1881. The house was bombed in 1943, resulting in a somewhat incoherent restoration, but the collection had been moved to safety.

voyage.name: Via Dante
voyage.content: One of the grandest and most frequented fashionable high streets in Milan. The Via Dante, named after the poet, is a beautiful and debonair pedestrian avenue which goes from the busy Piazzale Cordusio, all the way to the Largo Cairoli, just in front of the city castle. With loads of street vendors, restaurant and cafe tables, and often, street art, glamorous boutiques and often bustling with people, it's great for an

voyage.name: Corso Vittorio Emanuele II
voyage.content: One of the most popular high street shopping arteries in the city. It has a very elegant modern appearance, but too has some well-preserved grand 18th- and 19th-century buildings, including a rotunda-like neoclassical church. The Corso contains some great retail stores, including big shopping centres, fashionable outlets, and youthful, sporty designer boutiques. It is pedestrian.

voyage.name: Via Manzoni
voyage.content: Impressive refined-air street lined with aristocratic apartment blocks and opulent churches. It also hosts the Poldi Pezzoldi museum. Today, it is also one of the city's premier shopping streets, and is noted for containing the Armani Megastore. It is very close to La Scala opera house.

voyage.name: Via della Spiga
voyage.content: Lovely and classy little cobblestone street, with some beautiful ancient buildings. The street and its neighbourhood are more famous for the center of high-class shopping, where almost every luxury brand can be found.

voyage.name: Via Montenapoleone
voyage.content: The city's top high fashion shopping street. It contains many of the biggest names in fashion, and some of the trendiest and famous emporia and designer stores in the world. Today, despite containing mainly fashion boutiques, there are also some jewellery shops and cafes scattered here and there.

voyage.name: Viale Beatrice d'Este
voyage.content: Viale Beatrice d'Este is a street in the center of Milan, which is a 1 kilometer walk from Piazza del Duomo, begins in piazzale di Porta Lodovica and ends at the ancient Porta Vigentina, continuing with the name of viale Angelo Filippetti. It is a tree-lined avenue, which is connected in its continuation with viale Regina Margherita and viale Majno.The street is named after Princess Beatrice d'Este, Duchess of Milan

voyage.name: Piazza del Duomo
voyage.content: The grandest square in the city, the Piazza del Duomo is the cultural and social heart of Milan, and contains several of its most famous sights. There's the majestic cathedral and classy Galleria, plus the 18th C Palazzo Reale and several big, venerable buildings. The square is centred around the statue of King Victor Emmanuel II at Solferino – his horse is skidding to a halt as if it's just noticed the Austrian bayo

voyage.name: Piazza dei Mercanti
voyage.content: A truly enchanting and tiny medieval square, hidden by the grand palaces in the central part of Milan. Here, in "Merchants' Square" you get lovely Gothic and Renaissance-porticoed houses, and a well right in the middle. At the one side of the square there is the Palazzo della Ragione (1233), the old town hall, aka Broletto Nuovo. At the other – Loggia degli Osii (1321) decorated with black and white marble, used to h

voyage.name: Piazzale Cordusio
voyage.content: A central and busy square in Milan, right near the Duomo. It boasts some grand and beautiful late-19th-century architecture. Once, and to some extent still today, it was an economic hub of the city, with the headquarters of several companies, and big banks and postal offices.

voyage.name: Piazza Belgiojoso
voyage.content: A small, yet very impressive square, which hosts the magnificent neoclassical Belgiojoso Palace, built by Milanese noblemen in the late 1700s, and the House of Manzoni, where notable Italian writer and literary figure Alessandro Manzoni lived, and which today hosts a library and the Centro Nazionale di Studi Manzoniani (National Centre of Manzoni-related studies).

voyage.name: Piazza Della Scala
voyage.content: The location of the Statue of Leonardo da Vinci and La Scala theatre. It is a small, but grand square flanked by fine palaces, such as the city hall and the commercial bank. Great place for a photograph and right next to Galleria Vittorio Emanuele. Ticket office is underground in the Duomo Metropolitana stop.

voyage.name: Piazza San Babila
voyage.content: Busy and modern square just north of the cathedral and near the city's fashion district. Architecturally, Piazza San Babila's buildings are virtually all Art-Deco office blocks from the 1930s, but it has a trendy business and cosmopolitan feel to it, and despite being very modern, boasts a very old sight, San Babila, a tiny, pretty, Romanesque church standing shadowed away by the huge modern skyscrapers. Piazza San B

voyage.name: Piazza del Liberty
voyage.content: Small square, which however, is noted for a stunning Art Nouveau palace today called the Hotel del Corso, but once the Trianon. You reach it just off a tiny opening at the beginning of the Corso Vittorio Emanuele.

voyage.name: Piazzale Cadorna
voyage.content: Medium-sized, normal square in central Milan with the funky modern North Station and some fine buildings, but notably a set of peculiar modern sculptures in the middle.

voyage.name: Castello Sforzesco
voyage.content: "See who's in charge!" The round corner towers of the castle are two fists smacked down on the city plains, while the central square tower stares balefully down towards city centre. Who'd dare challenge the Duke? Yet so confident is he, he's built an extra redoubt within those walls, the military design is already outdated by the 15th century, and that rasping noise is his own family sharpening their knives against h

voyage.name: Old Hospital
voyage.content: A Renaissance complex which now serves the university.

voyage.name: Biblioteca Nazionale Braidense
voyage.content: A library established in 1770 by the Austrian governor. It has since acquired other historical collections and the archives of RAI (Italy's state television). It is very active in organising workshops and debates on new media and new technologies.

voyage.name: Torre Velasca
voyage.content: A tall, huge, castle-like skyscraper built in the 1950s, and one of the first in Italy. Stunning modern architecture. Unfortunately it is not possible to go on top, since it is a private building.

voyage.name: Expo Gate
voyage.content: Information hub and ticket office for the Expo Milano 2015. The gate consists of two structures designed by Scandurra Studio.

voyage.name: L.O.V.E. sculpture
voyage.content: On the square, where the Italian Stock exchange has its headquarters. The abbreviation L.O.V.E. stands for Libertà, Odio, Vendetta, Eternità (Freedom, Hate, Vengeance, Eternity) ideated by Maurizio Cattelan in his atelier on Viale Bligny in Milan.

voyage.name: Teatro alla Scala
voyage.content: One of the most renowned opera houses in the world. It first opened in 1778 and re-opened in 2004 after extensive renovation. It has seen performances by stars such as Maria Callas and Pavarotti. Since Italy is the birthplace of opera, The Teatro alla Scala would be one of the best places for one to have an introduction to the world of Italian opera. La Scala is also a venue for other classical music.

voyage.name: Teatro dal Verme
voyage.content: Classical music.

voyage.name: Galleria Vittorio Emanuele
voyage.content: The mother of all shopping malls: upscale shops in a splendid 19th century palace of a mall, with a stunning mosaic floor, and wonderful glass roof and cupola. Contains boutiques such as Louis Vuitton and Prada, a McDonald's fast-food restaurant, a silverware store called Bernasconi, and eating places such as the Zucca in Galleria, Biffi or a Gucci cafe (and loads more, notably art galleries, fashion boutiques, books

voyage.name: Armani Megastore
voyage.content: Giorgio Armani's flagship store. Covering over with outlets for his high-fashion creations, the Emporio Armani and Armani Jeans lines, plus the new Armani Casa selection of home furnishings, and flower, book, and art shops; a high-tech Sony electronics boutique/play centre in the basement; and an Emporio Café and branch of New York's Nobu sushi bar.

voyage.name: Dolce e Gabbana
voyage.content: High-end designer store dedicated to women's wear.

voyage.name: Gucci Flagship
voyage.content: This is Gucci's flagship store in the city, opened in 2002, which has high fashion clothing and accessories. There are also some other Gucci stores in Milan, including the Galleria Vittorio Emanuele, and even in Milan's Malpensa airport.

voyage.name: Prada
voyage.content: One of Prada's several boutiques in the city, the one in the Galleria is the closest to the Duomo and the central square. It sells a variety of high-fashion items, such as shoes, perfume, handbags, and accessories, both classical and modern, in a chandelier-filled, multi-floored shop (it is bigger than it looks from the outside).

voyage.name: Etro
voyage.content: Boutique store carrying the mens and womenswear line from high end label Etro.

voyage.name: La Rinascente
voyage.content: A big department store in Milan, right in the centre of the city near the Cathedral and Galleria, and very close to the chic Montenapoleone shopping zone. Here you can get houseware, design and appliances, male, female and children's fashion, youthful sports clothes, jewellery, accessories, cosmetics, watches, perfumes, glasses, socks, underwear, lingerie, gifts, table decor, a hair stylist, a restaurant, sushi bar,

voyage.name: D Magazine
voyage.content: This shop, in one of the most exclusive shopping streets in Milan, and in the world, is an outlet where you can find a lot of designer clothes. Names such as Giorgio Armani, Prada or Fendi can be found.

voyage.name: Peck
voyage.content: Foodies in the Duomo area should not miss this place. It is the Dean and Deluca of Milan, a gorgeous food shop that stocks the finest of just about everything. The prices are high, but since everything is counter service, you can graze a wide variety of delicacies for your money. Speaking of counter service, there is a special way to buy things at Peck. First, you order from the counter. They give you a little receip

voyage.name: Luna Rossa
voyage.content: A pizza restaurant.

voyage.name: Spontini
voyage.content: Pizza.

voyage.name: Il panino del laghetto
voyage.content: Sandwiches.

voyage.name: Pizzeria Gino Sorbillo
voyage.content: Probably the best pizza in town at a reasonable price. The restaurant reopens for dinner at 19:00, people will be lining up in front of the entrance beforehand (because the pizza is so good). Come early to avoid waiting!

voyage.name: Biffi
voyage.address: Passaggio Duomo, no. 2 (Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II)
voyage.content: Opened in 1867, it is an old fashioned restaurant/café in the Galleria Vittorio Emanuele, surrounded by a plethora of interesting shops, which serves drinks, and foods such as spaghetti, veal, steak, fish, and desserts such as chocolate Sacher, Tiramisu, ice cream and fruit salads. The waiters serve in the formal white gloves.

voyage.name: Terra e Mare
voyage.content: Sea food restaurant with specialities such as grilled swordfish and oysters on the menu.

voyage.name: Armani/Nobu
voyage.content: Part of Japanese restaurant chain serving sushi with South American influences in Armani-themed surroundings. Apart from sushi, dishes such as ceviche, spicy tuna, different soups, lobster, seaweed, salmon, or different forms of vegetables and meat (and several others) are on the menu, and you can find desserts such as carrot cakes, tea ice creams, chocolates, exotic fruits, or different, both European and oriental p

voyage.name: Savini
voyage.content: Opened in 1867, the Savini is a fancy and well-established restaurant inside the magnificent Galleria, serving meals such as Milanese-style risotto, spaghetti and ravioli, meat cutlet, lamb and beef, different forms of fish, warmly-made Tirmisu, and other forms of desserts including chocolate cake and tart with strawberries.

voyage.name: Tram restaurant ATMosfera
voyage.hours: departures for dinner daily at 20:00/20:30 and for lunch on sundays at 13:00/13:15
voyage.content: ATM, which operates the public transport in Milan, has created a tram restaurant. A tram of the class "Carrello" from 1928 has been transformed into a restaurant on tracks and you can have dinner and see many of Milan's sights at the same time.

voyage.name: Bar Magenta
voyage.content: This popular bar is best visited with a bunch of friends during apperitivo, a time when free appetizers are given out, usually around 19:00. It was said that Bar Magenta coined the now very popular “aperitivo”, and having a drink in here is a classic experience.

voyage.name: Caffè Cova
voyage.content: Founded in 1817, this pasticceria (pastry shop) relocated to the exclusive Montenapoleone street in 1950, and is a good place for a cake/tart with a hot drink, such as coffee. At Christmas, enjoy the traditional Panettone cake.

voyage.name: Emporio Armani Caffè
voyage.content: Found on the ground floor of the Armani Megastore, this café is all Armani themed. It's a good place to stop for a drink after a day of shopping, since it is really close to the ritzy Via Manzoni and Via Monte Napoleone.

voyage.name: Dolce e Gabbana Martini Bar
voyage.content: A Dolce & Gabbana themed bar, it is in the posh Venezia avenue, right in the top fashion district. Good place to enjoy a Martini cocktail in Dolce & Gabbana surroundings after some shopping or sightseeing.

voyage.name: Bar Jamaica
voyage.content: A small, trendy and artsy bar in the bohemian Brera district, which in summer times uses its verandah for open-air drinks.

voyage.name: Gucci café
voyage.content: If you enjoy cafés where you can sip fashionably at a coffee in the city's stunning glass Galleria, right in the heart of Milan, after some sightseeing or general shopping, then the Gucci café is the place to go.

voyage.name: Hotel Centrale
voyage.content: Nice but rather basic hotel near the central station.

voyage.name: Hotel Galileo Milan
voyage.price: €130 for single and €140 for a double. Rates include breakfast.
voyage.content: A four-star hotel with a choice of 89 single, double, triple and VIP rooms, all with private bath. Among the public areas are a bar, restaurant, lounge and reception with free internet connection.

voyage.name: Brunelleschi Hotel Milan
voyage.content: 4-star hotel.

voyage.name: Hotel Genius Milan
voyage.price: The rates change according to the season: single €88-99, double €120-155
voyage.content: 3-star hotel with 38 bedrooms with private en suite service and Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Hotel Lloyd
voyage.content: Offers large meeting rooms and a well-being program.

voyage.name: Santa Sofia Radisson
voyage.price: €311 for a double. Rates include breakfast.
voyage.content: A five-star luxury hotel. Among the public areas are a bar, restaurant, lounge and reception with free internet connection.

voyage.name: Palazzo Touring Radisson
voyage.price: €402 for a double. Rates include breakfast.
voyage.content: A five-star luxury hotel. Among the public areas are a bar, restaurant, lounge and reception with free internet.

voyage.name: Park Hyatt Milan
voyage.content: 5-star hotel that hosts La Cupola, a prominent restaurant.

voyage.name: Hotel De La Ville
voyage.content: Rooftop pool offers views of the Duomo.

voyage.name: Hotel Pierre Milano
voyage.content: Each of the 52 rooms has Wi-Fi access and satellite television.

voyage.name: Ariston Hotel Milan
voyage.content: 3-star hotel with 52 bedrooms (single, double and triple), private parking, a wine bar, a breakfast hall and a conference room able to host up to 25 people. Private baths, satellite TV, free internet access and a bike service.

voyage.name: Hotel King
voyage.content: 4-star hotel, part of the Mokinba Hotels.

voyage.name: Antica Locanda dei Mercanti
voyage.content: With/without private terraces. Large double rooms. In an old palazzo. Charming boutique hotel.

voyage.name: Santa Marta Suites
voyage.content: Boutique hotel with restaurant and panoramic terrace. 5 rooms and 5 suites.

voyage.name: La Rotonda della Besana
voyage.content: An 18th-century Neoclassical complex. It is now an exhibition space.

voyage.name: Porta Ticinese
voyage.content: A 19th-century gate and the surrounding area is a very old-fashioned quarter nearly untouched by World War II bombings.

voyage.name: Porta Romana
voyage.content: The southeastern city gate, the "gate towards Rome" is simpler built than Ticinese. However Milan has had a "Porta Romana" as a part of its city walls already when the city was part of the Roman Empire. It has given the name to the district it's in, and to the nearby Metro station.

voyage.name: Chiesa di Santa Maria delle Grazie al Naviglio
voyage.content: This landmark at the northern bank of Naviglio Grande bears the same name as the UNESCO World Heritage Site in the Western part of the country. The church is just a little over a century old, built in Romanesque Revival style, and is the third church built on that place.

voyage.name: Santa Maria al Paradiso
voyage.content: Built in the late 16th century for the Third Order of Saint Francis, much of its interior including decoration and paintings has been preserved.

voyage.name: Santa Maria presso San Celso
voyage.content: A late 15th-century church and sanctuary with many works of Milanese Baroque and Renaissance artists.

voyage.name: Gardens of the Guastalla
voyage.content: Among Milan's oldest (founded in the 16th century), but quite small gardens, and are very close to the University district. The parks, however, were only opened to the public in the early 20th century. You can have a nice walk inside, and you also have a classical temple-like structure and also a sort of pond with a Baroque railing surrounding it. Reachable via Crocetta, P.ta Romana, Missori or even San Babila metro

voyage.name: Basilicas Park
voyage.alt: Parco Papa Giovanni Paolo II or Parco delle Basiliche
voyage.content: Named the Basilicas Park as it connects two basilicas: the Basilica of San Lorenzo and the Basilica of Sant'Eustorgio. Formerly a place for drug use and anti-social behavior, it has been cleaned up and redesigned and is now more pleasant. It was renamed after the late Pope John Paul II.

voyage.name: Parco Vittorio Formentano
voyage.content: A park with many different trees in the southeast of Milan at the location of a former market. The park also hosts the building of , where theater performances and concerts are held.

voyage.name: Auditorium di Milano
voyage.content: The seat of the Verdi orchestra with a program of classical and modern music.

voyage.name: Osteria del Gnocco Fritto
voyage.content: At Osteria del Gnocco Fritto the €4.50 cover charge includes baskets of fried hand-size pastries (similar to sopapillas) accompanied by meats, cheeses, or jams (€8-11). The restaurant has a second location further southwest.

voyage.name: Cow Burger
voyage.content: Very small place with great Italian-style burgers. Customized burgers available.

voyage.name: Lacerba
voyage.content: For an artistic dining experience, try Lacerba on via dei Orti, 4, which serves dishes inspired by the early 20th-century art movement, Futurism.

voyage.name: Osteria dei Formaggi
voyage.content: The Osteria dei Formaggi on the Grand Canal serves all manner of excellent cheese dishes in an intimate dining room heavily decorated with cows.

voyage.name: El Brellin
voyage.content: For a classic take on Milanese cooking, try Ill Brellin, where you can choose from homey classics such as rigatoni sautéed with pancetta, to modern interpretations on typical ingredients—a pumpkin tart as an appetizer. Outdoor seating makes this a perfect choice on a sunny day, although it is closed for dinner on Sundays.

voyage.name: Rita
voyage.content: It is the perfect place for a cocktail and Edo, the barman and the owner together with the chief Luca, is the grandmaster. They have strict code for preparing cocktails: no syrups are admitted, only fresh fruit. It is also a perfect place to eat.

voyage.name: Cicco Simonetta
voyage.content: A bohemian pub hosting comics, musicians, and €3 beer on Mondays.

voyage.name: Black Hole
voyage.content: A former lesbian club.

voyage.name: Hotel Romana Residence Milan
voyage.price: Double and twin rooms €159, breakfast included
voyage.content: The Romana Residence modern hotel of the historic centre of Milan, 250 metres away from the Duomo. All the 66 bedrooms of the Romana Residence Hotel, divided in double, twin, triple, family, junior suite and suite, come with private bath and modern facilities. Some also have a small kitchen, and many face the garden of the hotel.

voyage.name: Aquae Calidae – Milano
voyage.content: Aquae Calidae - L’hotel dispone di un moderno e spazioso centro benessere, sala fitness, ristorante e salone di bellezza.

voyage.name: Leonardo da Vinci Museum of Science and Technology
voyage.alt: Museo Nazionale della Scienza e della Tecnologia
voyage.price: €10, concessions €7.50, disabled and children under 3 free. Guided tours €8 or €10 with reservation
voyage.content: As the name tells, it is a museum to learn more about science and technology. Hosted in a former monastery, San Vittore al Corpo.

voyage.name: Triennale
voyage.price: Adult €10; student, under 26 or senior €8.50; child up to 16 free
voyage.content: Museum of Design and Architecture, always has 4-6 exhibits on the subject of design, photography or modern art, at least 1-2 of which are always free entry.

voyage.name: Saint Mary of the Graces
voyage.content: Houses the famous Last Supper ('Cenacolo Vinciano') by Leonardo da Vinci. It is best to reserve tickets a few months before the visit. Canceled reservations are sold from 08:15 every morning (if there are any, best to show up in person). The church and the painting are inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List. If you arrive without tickets, you can buy a pass to five DaVinci museums for €38 that will get you in to

voyage.name: Palazzo del Sole 24 ore
voyage.content: An office building hosting the business magazine Sole 24 Ore and an example of modern Italian architecture.

voyage.name: Deposito Tranviario Messina
voyage.content: The tram deposit is an example of early 20th-century Italian industrial architecture with an impressive iron gridded ceiling.

voyage.name: Villa Simonetta
voyage.content: A 15th-century Renaissance villa with a massive loggia. The villa has functioned as a candle factory, opera house and hospital, now hosting a music school.

voyage.name: Cimitero Monumentale
voyage.content: Milan's old cemetery in Neoclassical style. It is filled with lavish sculptures, impressive mausoleums and monuments. Well worth a visit!

voyage.name: Arco della Pace
voyage.content: The triumphal arch of peace stands at the place at one of Milan's seven city gates. First the gate was known as Porta Giovia and was closer to the city center. Porta Sempione means "Gate towards Simplon", and once the road leading over the Simplon Pass to Paris went through this gate. The current gate was built in the early 19th century and at that time it was referred to as Arco della Pace.

voyage.name: Sempione Park
voyage.content: A big space of green land right behind the Sforzesco castle, and one of the most famous and popular in the city. Designed in like a neoclassical landscape garden, there are loads of features - such as a lake, the aforementioned arch of peace, a Roman-style sports' amphitheatre, a tower (which today hosts the Just Cavalli Hollywood), and several interesting features. It's a lovely leafy place to enjoy a walk at any ti

voyage.name: Corso Magenta
voyage.content: An elegant and aristocratic street in the north-western part of Milan. It contains sophisticated cafes and shops, and also some fine, mainly Baroque, palaces, notably the Palazzo Litta, one of the best examples of 18th century Milanese architecture, and also a place in which Napoleon I spent some time. Metro stations Conciliazione, Cadorna, Cairoli and Cordusio are the closest to the avenue. The famous Santa Maria de

voyage.name: Chinatown
voyage.content: Not as big or famous as the ones in London or New York, Milan does also have a Chinatown, dating from the 1920s. Main street is the Via Paolo Sarpi, which is mainly a pedestrian street. Wide varieties of Chinese food is available. See Eat section for specific recommendations.

voyage.name: Hadid Residences
voyage.content: Designed by Zaha Hadid and completed but not yet in use.

voyage.name: Libeskind Residences
voyage.content: Designed by Daniel Libeskind and constructions are completed.

voyage.name: Allianz Tower (Torre Isozaki)
voyage.content: It is not accessible, but since it is 207 m high with 50 floors you can see it from far away. Designed by Arata Isozaki.

voyage.name: Torre Branca
voyage.content: The tower is 108 m high built in 1933 and designed by architect Giò Ponti. From here you can get good views over Milan.

voyage.name: Pizzeria Da Giuliano
voyage.content: Nice and cozy pizzeria with great, quite thick and large pizza slices. You can choose your toppings and after a few minutes you'll get your slice. Wood burning oven and loads of Mozzarella.

voyage.name: La Ravioleria Sarpi
voyage.content: Maybe the best place to have Chinese dumplings in Italy. Many selections available (pork, beef or vegetarian). They also sell a Chinese version of crêpes. Only takeaway.

voyage.name: Ciripizza
voyage.content: Another very yummy pizza restaurant with reasonable prices. Eat in or takeaway. English menu available.

voyage.name: Just Cavalli
voyage.address: Via Luigi Camoens (inside the Torre Branca, Parco Sempione)
voyage.content: Found inside the Torre Branca in the big, leafy Sempione park, the Just Cavalli Hollywood was the brainchild of Roberto Cavalli, the fashion designer. It was renovated in 2009-10. For beginners, one can find cheese, tuna tartar, Parma ham, and caviar, and for the main course, you can eat dishes of spaghetti, risotto, small gnocchi with crab, different forms of seafood, veal, steak, and different forms of salads. It a

voyage.name: Bar Bianco
voyage.content: It's cash only at this bar, but with Gucci-clad clubbers and their well-suited companions, money seems easy to come by. The life of a party can always be detected in here.

voyage.name: Honky Tonks
voyage.content: Not exactly a country cowboy bar as the name might imply, a more accurate description would include the smoky lounge feel and the jazz music being played. The drinks are well made and they also serve Tex-Mex style food.

voyage.name: Roialto
voyage.content: Its bland façade conceals a real gem of a cocktail bar/restaurant. It is a very popular spot for after-work drinks, or perhaps a pre-club drink if you're going dancing somewhere like the Gattopardo.

voyage.name: Hotel Panizza
voyage.content: 3-star hotel in central Milan Magenta district, offers 22 rooms at affordable rates.

voyage.name: Hotel Capitol
voyage.content: A 66-room 4-star hotel near the Exhibition centre, the Financial district, the airport shuttle terminal, and the underground station.

voyage.name: Society for Fine Arts and Permanent Exhibition
voyage.alt: Società per la Belle Arti ed Esposizione Permanente
voyage.content: Changing exhibitions of contemporary art.

voyage.name: Contemporary Arts Pavilion
voyage.hours: Tue Wed Fri-Sun 09:30-19:30; Thu 09:30-22:30; Mon closed
voyage.content: A contemporary art space. In 1993 a bomb destroyed the building in a time when Italy was heavily committed in its fight against the Mafia.

voyage.name: Modern Art Gallery
voyage.content: Mainly features 19th-century Italian art.

voyage.name: Natural Science Museum
voyage.price: Has reduced and free entry (depends on person) after 16:30 most days or 14:30 Fridays

voyage.name: Boschi Di Stefano House Museum
voyage.content: Extensive collection of 20th century art. Building (1929–1931) and some furniture by Piero Portaluppi.

voyage.name: Piazza Duca d'Aosta
voyage.content: A very big, relatively modern and busy square in the north-east of Milan, famous for hosting the city's majestic central station, and the Pirelli skyscraper. The Piazza is generally bustling with people, and is at the heart of Milan's economic and business district. It is where you'll end up if you need to go to the central station, but it is also a good place to go because it boasts some excellent examples of post-S

voyage.name: Piazza della Repubblica
voyage.content: A modern and very busy square north-west of Milan. It contains some of the most important office blocks and company buildings in the country, and boasts some good examples of 1950s and 60s Italian architecture. The square is an important one for transportation, and contains some grand hotels. It is also close to the Piazza Duca d'Aosta and the city Central station.

voyage.name: Corso Venezia
voyage.content: Considered one of the finest and most beautiful streets in the city. Right near the glitzy Montenapoleone area, it is flanked by a series of beautiful villas, museums and palazzi, from all eras. It also contains parts of the Giardini Pubblici, an old and leafy garden and park. On addition to being an aristocratic-aired place, today, several elegant boutiques have opened up here, so it's great for both sight-seeing an

voyage.name: Corso Buenos Aires
voyage.content: One of the longest shopping streets in Italy and Europe. It is a large avenue, who, at first, is quite old, but the buildings gradually become newer further along. Today, it contains loads, loads and loads of shops, such as Swarovsky, H&M, Milano House of Cashmere, Calzedonia, Outlet, United Colors of Benetton, Adidas, Nike, Calvin Klein, Zara, Luisa Spagnoli, and a good number more. Since the Corso Buenos Aires is s

voyage.name: Porta Nuova
voyage.content: The Napoleonic "new gate" is located next to the modern business district and is simpler built than the other city gates. You might pass through if walking from the central station to Duomo.

voyage.name: Porta Venezia
voyage.content: Known by its current name since 1862, this gate has origins that can be traced back to the Roman Empire. The current rather massive gate structure consists of two buildings and was completed in 1828.

voyage.name: Porta Garibaldi
voyage.content: Yet another gate from the early 19th century that has lent its name to the district around it and to the nearby railway station.

voyage.name: Giardini Pubblici Indro Montanelli
voyage.content: An 18th-century park complex in the Montenapoleone/Porta Venezia district, designed in an English Romantic garden style. Inside, you can find rockeries, water features, fountains, statues and monuments, and other interesting features. You also get a planetarium, a natural history museum, and on the other side of the Palestro street, you can also find an opulent Royal villa which today hosts a contemporary art collect

voyage.name: Torre Unicredit
voyage.content: The tallest building in Italy by virtue of its 84-metre spire on top of 146 metres of office floors, completed in 2011 to serve as the headquarters of the Unicredit bank.

voyage.name: Palazzo Lombardia
voyage.content: The government of the region of Lombardy spared little expense to relocate itself to what became Italy's tallest building when completed in 2010. It ceded this title to Torre Unicredit one year later, but has an upper hand in terms of the highest usable floor at 160 metres. The building is open for visit every Sunday, from 10:00 to 18:00. During visit time, you can climb to the "belvedere" glass wall on the 39th floo

voyage.name: Torre Solaria
voyage.content: The tallest residential building in Italy. The unmistakable Jenga-like visage of the tower is achieved by alternating balconies to offer better views and privacy.

voyage.name: Pirelli Tower
voyage.content: Completed in 1956, the Pirelli Tower became a turning point in the history of global architecture, even though its looks may pale now in comparison to the newer postmodern-era towers, as well as a symbol of the rebound of Milan and the Italian economy following the Second World War. It was built by the Pirelli company known for tire manufacturing, and was the seat of government the Region of Lombardy until it moved t

voyage.name: Bosco Verticale
voyage.content: The residential twin tower's name should be interpreted literally, as it stems from the fact that the buildings' intricate facades contain actual living trees on various levels, which serve a variety of purposes beneficial to the residents. The total amount of vegetation growing on the facades is equivalent to a hectare of an actual forest.

voyage.name: Torre Galfa
voyage.content: The name "Galfa" is a portmanteau derived from the names of the two streets where the tower has its facades, Via Galvani and Via Fara.

voyage.name: Villa Necchi Campiglio
voyage.alt: owned by FAI - Italian National Trust
voyage.price: €15. Free entry with the Case Museo (house museums) card. Free entry to the bar/restaurant and garden
voyage.content: Built by Piero Portaluppi from 1932 to 1935 for the industrial Necchi Campiglio family, it also has a beautiful garden.

voyage.name: Conservatorio di musica Giuseppe Verdi
voyage.content: It is a university for the musicians of the future and concerts by them are held in the Verdi (about 1000 seats) and Puccini halls.

voyage.name: Corso Buenos Aires
voyage.content: Connects Porta Venezia to Piazzale Loreto, and is the place to go for fashion shopping: here you can find Calzedonia, Alex Fashion, Luisa Spagnoli, Furla, Brian & Barry and Nara Camice.

voyage.name: 10 Corso Como
voyage.content: Found in the early 1990s, this sort of "multi-functional" shopping complex is found in the same place as its name. Considered a lifestyle emporium and 13,000 square feet big, it contains some fashion shops, design, photography and art gallery, luxury goods, a bookshop, accessories, a cafe and a restaurant. Situated in the Garibaldi district, near the Centro Direzionale (Milan's business district), it has a courtyard,

voyage.name: Eataly Milan Smeraldo
voyage.content: Eataly is a gourmet grocery store associated with Slow movement. It styles itself as a place to "savor high quality traditional Italian food products and beverages along with local produce and artisanal products." Many different products are for sale, including not only produce but cheese, wine, olive oil, and sweets, and there are also several places to eat hot food. Anyone who enjoys shopping or window-shopping for

voyage.name: Pianeta Luna
voyage.content: A self service restaurant near the Central Railway Station, with pizza, pasta and other classic Italian dishes and English speaking staff. Very reasonable prices and good food combined with a wide variety of wines - this is not a tourist trap.

voyage.name: Pizzeria Fashion 2
voyage.content: Pizza Fashion near the Centrale train station is good choice and they also do takeaway dessert if you're running to catch your train.

voyage.name: Pizzeria Spontini
voyage.content: Nice pizza in a small restaurant with very economical prices.

voyage.name: Caffé Panzera
voyage.content: A lively Italian restaurant with decent ossobuco, pizza and other dishes at about €15 and delicious desserts.

voyage.name: Trattoria Siciliana da Salvatore
voyage.content: Dishes from Sicily, mostly fish and seafood. Try the swordfish!

voyage.name: Il Canarino
voyage.content: Expect to find typical local dishes on the menu like risotto alla milanese and ossobuco. They have a five courses menu that is a bit expensive but worth the money.

voyage.name: Al Matarel
voyage.content: Specializing in Paduan cuisine with dishes like ossobuco con risotto.

voyage.name: La Terrazza
voyage.content: For a Mediterranean take on Japanese cuisine, head to La Terraza which serves fusion food among a contemporary decor. During the summer months, everyone heads to the terrace, where you can see the treetops of the nearby Giardini Pubblici. There's a "happy hour" every day except Sunday; on Sunday, brunch is served.

voyage.name: Giannino
voyage.content: A refined restaurant from 1899 serving meals such as mozzarella, Parma ham, mussels, salad, Milanese-style risotto, spaghetti, soup, beef, chicken, scampi.

voyage.name: Fashion Café
voyage.content: Fashionable Armani-style place for aperitivo and drinks.

voyage.name: b:free cocktail bar
voyage.content: If you want to visit a real Aperitivo bar in true Italian fashion, this is a worthy hot spot.

voyage.name: Brasserie Bruxelles
voyage.content: A bar specialising in beer from Belgium. 5 beer on draught and 50 in the bottle.

voyage.name: L'Elephant
voyage.content: Wednesday and Thursday nights hosts a gay crowd at L'elephant

voyage.name: Boston Hotel Milan
voyage.content: Elegant two-star hotel with 25 single, double and triple bedrooms with private bath, shower, Wi-Fi connection and air conditioning.

voyage.name: Dover Hotel Milan
voyage.content: Thirteen single, double/twin and triple accommodations with en-suites services, internet connections, TV and telephone.

voyage.name: Hotel Delle Nazioni
voyage.content: 3-star hotel 400 metres from the main railway station.

voyage.name: Hotel Garda
voyage.price: Singles from €45 to €150. Doubles from €75 to €225

voyage.name: NH Milano Touring
voyage.content: This 4-star hotel, surrounded by many famous monuments, has 282 rooms, a restaurant, parking, Wi-Fi and a bar.

voyage.name: Berna Swiss Quality Hotel
voyage.price: Single room from €89, double room from €116 (low season of 2009).
voyage.content: Four-star hotel 100 m away from the station.

voyage.name: Hotel Amadeus
voyage.price: The average rates are €80 but weekend rates for a single room can drop to as low as €42
voyage.content: Really close to the Centrale station.

voyage.name: Hotel Auriga Milan
voyage.content: The Auriga is a four-star hotel right in front of the central train station of Milan. It has 52 bedrooms, all with private bath, shower, TV and internet connection.

voyage.name: Hotel Canova
voyage.content: Cheapest booked via an intermediary, more expensive direct. Parking €20 per night, or use cheaper local garage. Excellent location near Stazione Centrale.

voyage.name: Hotel Casa Mia
voyage.price: Average prices: single rooms €65, doubles €90, triples €120.
voyage.content: 15 minutes' walk to the Duomo and 10 minutes to Via Montenapoleone, small and attentive.

voyage.name: Hotel Galles
voyage.price: Singles from €75, Queen size bed from €92, parking €21 per night

voyage.name: Residence de la Gare
voyage.price: Executive Apartment for one week from €770.

voyage.name: UNA Tocq Boutique Hotel
voyage.content: Offers 109 rooms and 13 apartments right in the heart of Corso Como. The hotel also features a restaurant and bar, a fitness center with indoor swimming pool, and a garage nearby the hotel.

voyage.name: Best Western Hotel Felice Casati
voyage.content: 4-star hotel.

voyage.name: Crowne Plaza Milan City
voyage.content: 4-star hotel offers 99 rooms plus a wellness and fitness center, restaurant, bar, meeting rooms, suites and family rooms.

voyage.name: Hotel Andreola Central
voyage.content: Four-star hotel 200 m from the central train station.

voyage.name: Hotel Baviera
voyage.content: Classic 4-star hotel.

voyage.name: Casa Baglioni Milan
voyage.content: 5-star boutique hotel in the Brera district, inspired by 1960s Milanese design. Features stylish rooms with custom furnishings and modern bathrooms. Breakfast is included.

voyage.name: Chiaravalle Abbey
voyage.content: A beautifully-preserved medieval abbey still run by monks today.

voyage.name: San Cristoforo Sul Naviglio
voyage.content: A complex of two churches, the older one is built in the 13th century on a place where there has been houses of worship since the Roman Empire.

voyage.name: Paolo Pini Art Museum
voyage.content: Contemporary art gallery collection.

voyage.name: Hangar Bicocca
voyage.content: Contemporary art museum in a giant hangar in the industrial district just north of Milano Bicocca university. They have a few permanent sculptural installations along with rotating temporary exhibits and events.

voyage.name: Museo San Siro Collezione Milan Inter
voyage.content: Inter and Milan paraphernalia are at display at the museum in the stadium that two of the most famous football (soccer) teams in Italy call home.

voyage.name: Leonardo's Horse
voyage.content: A bronze sculpture realised according to an original project of Leonardo da Vinci. It is on the courtyard of the race-track of San Siro, just behind the Stadium. The race-track is open on race days but the courtyard is open everyday.

voyage.name: Certosa di Garegnano
voyage.content: The Garegnano Charterhouse houses Capuchin Friars and 16th century frescoes.

voyage.name: Watch a football game at San Siro Stadium
voyage.content: Watch AC Milan or FC Internazionale at the famous Giuseppe Meazza Stadium, also known as San Siro, which is shared as a home stadium by both clubs. Tickets for most matches are available in advance or on the day. The rivalry between the two sides is very bitter, and considered to be one of the biggest in Italy, and matches between both sides, known as the Derby della Madonnina, are particularly charged affairs which

voyage.name: Sunbathing and do aquatic sports at the Idroscalo
voyage.content: Also known as "sea of Milan", the Idroscalo is an artificial lake in Milan. In this place you can practice many sports such as kayaking, canoeing, dragon boats, rowing, sailing, swimming, horse riding and water skiing. In Idroscalo park there are also bars and nightclubs and it is used for open-air concerts. Free wifi internet connection available. Near idroscalo there is Europark Idroscalo Milano, a family-oriented

voyage.name: Osteria del Gnocco Fritto
voyage.content: At Osteria del Gnocco Fritto the €4.50 cover charge includes baskets of fried hand-size pastries (similar to sopapillas) accompanied by meats, cheeses, or jams (€8 to €11). The restaurant has a second location closer to the city center.

voyage.name: La Trattoria Da Abele
voyage.content: Renowned for its risottos, which change seasonally, Da Abele has a relaxed atmosphere and place that is always packed with locals.

voyage.name: Dilemma
voyage.content: Restaurant & cocktail bar.

voyage.name: Birrificio Lambrate
voyage.content: Features with its own branded beers.

voyage.name: Sio Café
voyage.content: A disco north of the Central railway station.

voyage.name: Amnesia
voyage.content: Saturday nights at Billy or Amnesia,

voyage.name: Borgo del Tempo Perso
voyage.hours: open year-round although outdoor area open May-Sept only
voyage.content: On Sunday nights, hundreds flock to the largest and classiest spot in town, the Borgo del Tempo Perso.

voyage.name: Città di Milano
voyage.content: It is way on the outskirts of the city. If you arrive by car, take the tangenziale Ovest and exit at San Siro/ Fiera. If by public transport, take the subway (the M1 line to De Angeli) and then a bus (bus no 72). However keep an eye out for signs pointing to the campsite. Don't be afraid to ask locals on the bus where it is. Be aware that it's next to a rather smelly farm. However, the campsite itself has a bar, a re

voyage.name: Piero Rotta Youth Hostel
voyage.content: Follow the signs from QT8 stop on the red line to Molino Dorino. Very relaxed curfew compared to most in Italy. Look out for the night walkers you pass on the way to the hostel. 5 km from Duomo.

voyage.name: OstellOlinda
voyage.price: Price begins at €18/night, includes free wifi
voyage.content: Hostel converted from an old psychiatric ward, though other buildings on the grounds are still used for psychiatric treatment. Reception desk is only open from noon to 20:00, and the staff only speaks enough English to keep the place functioning. Entry after dark requires checking in with the gate guard. No curfew, but remember that the guard-gate is closed from 01:30 to 06:00. It is near the Affori Train Station. Ea

voyage.name: Hotel De Albertis
voyage.content: In the Cinque Giornate area. Run by a very pleasant family.

voyage.name: Hotel Delizia
voyage.price: Double room single use €60, two persons €120
voyage.content: Comfortable access to the tangenziale and the splendid Piazza del Duomo. 14 rooms each with shower, bidet, toilet, free Wi-Fi, TV, ADSL, breakfast.

voyage.name: Hotel Accursio
voyage.content: A small hotel, with only 28 rooms, but the location is convenient and the small breakfast service is nice.

voyage.name: Hotel Bonola
voyage.content: Hotel Bonola is close to the freeway exits (the Tangenziale Ovest exit "Viale Certosa" is 1 km away), "Rho-Pero", the new trade show center and Mazdapalace the historical trade show center.

voyage.name: Residenza Calvino Milan
voyage.content: 42 self-catering apartments for short vacations and stays. It is in the northern area of Milan. Services include the wi-fi internet connection, LCD TV, kitchen, bathroom and reception.

voyage.name: Dieci Hotel Milan
voyage.price: €150 for a double room, breakfast included.
voyage.content: Close to the Piola Metro stop, in the north-east part of the city. The 29 guest rooms are divided in single, double and triple, with en-suite services, satellite TV, internet connection and mini bar.

voyage.name: Hotel Florence
voyage.content: In northeastern Milan, easily reached from the Centrale station, with excellent public transport services (subway, street cars and buses) and full of attractions.

voyage.name: Milan Suite Hotel
voyage.content: Modern hotel in the north district, well connected to the city centre and Fiera Milano. 40 bedrooms divided in double for single use, suite and junior suite. All the rooms come with en-suite service and the breakfast included. Facilities include two meeting halls, private parking and limousine service.
